title: Additive ideal image equals tensor sections of the module quotient
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and J contained in I be quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Let r_K:A_X to (i_K)_*A_{Z_K} be the additive structure restriction [def-sc-etale-additive-structure-restriction]. Let F be the specified categorical module cokernel of J.toModules to I.toModules, and assume F is quasi-coherent. Then im(ker(r_I) to A_X to (i_J)_*A_{Z_J}) is isomorphic to ULift(F_et), where F_et is the tensor-sections sheaf [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. This assertion has no nilpotence or square-zero hypothesis.

proof.text: Refine by affine etale V over affine U=Spec A. With B=Gamma(V,O), the additive kernel for I is I_B and its restriction into B/J_B has kernel J_B. Hence its sectionwise image is I_B/J_B. These are the ideals cut out by the specified subscheme restrictions.

Flatness of B over A identifies I_B/J_B with B tensor_A coker(J(U) to I(U)). The specified ideal modules are the kernels of the same structure-module maps and the specified morphism is their inclusion. Affine sections of the tensor pullback of their specified cokernel are thus precisely this quotient.

The quotient maps, inclusion maps, and tensor base change commute with restriction ring maps; the local identifications and their inverses therefore glue. Categorical sheaf images are sheafifications of the presheaf images, giving the required isomorphism with tensor sections. Lift additive coefficients to the Gm universe. If I=J, I=0, or X is empty the same comparison is between zero sheaves.

      ((sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}).obj

          (cokernel (IdealSheafData.toModulesOfLE hJI)))))
